- The addition of `set_filename(NULL);` in `mobile-widgets/qmlmanager.cpp` complements the changes made in the other two files by ensuring that the filename is consistently reset across different contexts, particularly when handling cloud storage scenarios. This maintains the integrity of the application's state management after the changes made in the other files. 

Overall, these modifications enhance the separation of concerns and improve the clarity of file state management across the application.

Here is the commit message:
Move resetting of current file out of clear_dive_file_data()

This is the only case where C-code sets the current file.
Remove this call for a better separation of C-backend and
C++-frontend parts.

There were four callers of clear_dive_file_data(). Two of them
would call set_filename() anyway. For the remaining two add an
explicit call to set_filename().

This commit fixes a bug introduced in commit b3901aa8f90499ee2a34efdddc2463105afc53f1:
The cloud-online menu entry was still enabled after "closing" the
cloud storage.

Signed-off-by: Berthold Stoeger <bstoeger@mail.tuwien.ac.at>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `clear_dive_file_data()` function not resetting the `existing_filename`, which led to the cloud-online menu entry remaining enabled even after the cloud storage was "closed." This improper handling of the current file state allowed the application to incorrectly indicate that a cloud connection was still active.

Here is the patch:
 
 void clear_dive_file_data()
 {
 	while (dive_table.nr)
 		delete_single_dive(0);
 	while (dive_site_table.nr)
 		delete_dive_site(get_dive_site(0)->uuid);
 
 	clear_dive(&displayed_dive);
 	clear_dive_site(&displayed_dive_site);
 
-	free((void *)existing_filename);
-	existing_filename = NULL;
-
 	reset_min_datafile_version();
 	saved_git_id = "";
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
free((void *)existing_filename);
existing_filename = NULL;
```
Reason:
The `clear_dive_file_data()` function was responsible for clearing dive-related data but did not reset the `existing_filename` variable properly. This omission meant that even after the cloud storage was "closed," the application still retained a reference to the previous filename, causing the cloud-online menu entry to remain enabled incorrectly.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
set_filename(NULL);
```
Reason:
By explicitly calling `set_filename(NULL)` after clearing the dive file data, the code ensures that the `existing_filename` is reset appropriately. This change provides a clear separation between the C-backend and C++-frontend parts of the application, ensuring that the state of the current file is correctly updated, thus preventing the cloud-online menu entry from remaining enabled after closing the cloud storage.
